get.description:
Get all translations for a specific language as a cacheable key-value dictionary.

The `revision` parameter is required for cache busting - clients should use the current
max revision from `/translations/revision` endpoint.

**Supported languages:** en, ru, de, fr, es, it, pt

**Response format:**
```json
{
  "category.electronics": "Electronics",
  "feature.color": "Color",
  ...
}
```


**Permissions:** `ReadOnlyOrSuperUser`

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Language code (en, ru, de, fr, es, it, pt)

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: Current revision number (for cache busting). Get from /translations/revision endpoint.

post.description:
Translate a text — or a batch of short texts — into a configured language.

Send **either** `text` (one string) **or** `texts` (a list, order preserved,
translated in one provider call so a screen's copy keeps a consistent tone).
`source_lang` defaults to the module's `DEFAULT_LANGUAGE`; `context` is a
free-text domain hint that rides into the prompt.

Bounded on purpose — every miss spends real money on an LLM budget:
`TEXT_MAX_CHARS` per text (`error.400.translate.text_too_long`),
`TEXT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS` (`error.400.translate.batch_too_large`) and
`TEXT_BATCH_MAX_CHARS` (`error.400.translate.batch_too_long`) per batch,
throttled under scope `translate_text`, and cached for `TEXT_CACHE_TTL`
seconds under a digest of (source, target, context, text).

`text` in the response is `texts[0]` — the single-text form's answer, and a
convenience for it.

get.description:
List translations with revision-based pagination.

**Sync flow:**
1. Initial sync: Call without min_revision to get all translations
2. Store `revisions.global_max` from response
3. Subsequent syncs: Call with `min_revision={stored_max}` to get only changes


**Permissions:** `ReadOnlyOrSuperUser`

parameters.name: include_deleted
parameters.description: Include soft-deleted items in response. Default: true

parameters.name: max_revision
parameters.description: Return objects with revision less than or equal to this value (inclusive). Default: no limit

parameters.name: min_revision
parameters.description: Return objects with revision greater than this value (exclusive). Omit for initial sync to get all items.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Number of items per page. Default: 100, Max: 1000

get.description:
Mixin for ViewSets working with RevisionMixin models.

Provides:
- Automatic revision-based filtering
- OpenAPI documentation for revision query parameters
- Optional filtering of soft-deleted items
- /revision endpoint to get current max revision

Usage:
    class MyModelViewSet(RevisionViewSetMixin, viewsets.ModelViewSet):
        queryset = MyModel.objects.all()
        serializer_class = MyModelSerializer
        pagination_class = RevisionPagination

Query parameters:
- min_revision: Return objects with revision > min_revision (default: 0)
- max_revision: Return objects with revision <= max_revision (default: None)
- include_deleted: Include soft-deleted items (default: true)

**Permissions:** `ReadOnlyOrSuperUser`

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A unique integer value identifying this Translation.

post.description:
Bulk create or update translations. Provide an array of objects with a ``key`` and a ``values`` mapping: ``{"key": "a.b", "values": {"en": "Hello", "de": "Hallo"}}``.

**Permissions:** `IsSuperUser`

get.description:
Get all data as a cacheable JSON array.

The `revision` parameter is required for cache busting - clients should use the current
max revision from `/revision` endpoint. Response includes Cache-Control header for 30 days.

**Usage:**
1. Call `/revision` to get current max revision
2. Call `/data.json?revision={max_revision}` to get all data
3. Cache the response locally - it won't change until revision changes


**Permissions:** `ReadOnlyOrSuperUser`

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: Current revision number (for cache busting). Get from /revision endpoint.

Get the current maximum revision number for this resource.

**Permissions:** `ReadOnlyOrSuperUser`

TextTranslationRequest.description:
Request body of ``POST translate/api/v1/text/``.

Two shapes over one endpoint: ``text`` for a single string (a listing
description a viewer wants to read), ``texts`` for a batch of short ones
(a screen's worth of UI copy, translated together so the tone matches).
Exactly one of them; the length ceilings live in ``text.check_bounds``
so both shapes are bounded by the same numbers and refuse with the same
error codes.

text.description: A single text to translate. Mutually exclusive with `texts`.

texts.description: Several short texts to translate in one call, order preserved. Mutually exclusive with `text`.

target_lang.description: Language code to translate into; must be a configured language.

source_lang.description: Language code the texts are written in. Defaults to STAPEL_TRANSLATE['DEFAULT_LANGUAGE'].

context.description: Free-text context/domain hint ('a car listing title', 'legal copy'). Rides into the prompt and is part of the cache key.

TextTranslationResult.description: Content translation of one text or a batch of them (POST text/).

texts.description: Translations, in the order the texts were given

text.description: First translation — the answer of the single-text form

source_language.description: Source language, as given or defaulted

target_language.description: Language the texts were translated into

provider.description: Class name of the configured LLM provider

cached.description: Whether every returned text came from the cache

The full authoring row — privileged callers only.

Kept explicit rather than ``'__all__'`` so that adding a model column is
a decision about which surface it lands on, not an automatic publish.

screenshot.description: Screenshot of Figma screen where this key is used

llm_translated.description: Whether this translation was generated by LLM

TranslationEntryPublic.description:
The entry as an unauthenticated UI-string consumer sees it.

An allowlist, not an exclusion list: a column added to
``TranslationEntry`` tomorrow stays off this surface until somebody
names it here. The read endpoints are reachable anonymously
(``ReadOnlyOrSuperUser`` passes every SAFE_METHOD), so everything a
client does not need to render a string is authoring metadata that
would otherwise be published — developer comments, Figma refs of
unreleased designs, screenshot URLs, provenance flags.
